title: Stages of the bioeconomy of the production process Sitotroga cerealella
author: C A Zuniga-Gonzalez

steps.title: Wash Wheat Substrate
steps.instruction: Prepare the wheat raw material by washing and distributing it into pans.

substeps.instruction: Inspect wheat to ensure it is free of other grain varieties.
Weigh each bag of wheat and empty it into a plastic container (capacity > 45.36 kg).
Pour 25 liters of water into the tub until wheat is completely covered; let soak for 3 minutes.
Empty the water and distribute the wet wheat into pans, averaging 6.577089 kg per pan (approximately 7 pans per 45.36 kg).
Collect any spilled grains and place them in the final pan to avoid waste.

steps.title: Sterilize Wheat Substrate
steps.instruction: Heat-treat the wheat in an oven to sterilize the substrate.

substeps.instruction: Place pans in the oven, averaging 5 pans per shelf, ensuring uniform temperature distribution.
Turn on the oven and fan to reach an optimum temperature of 90°C over approximately 2 hours.
Maintain sterilization for a period of 8 hours.
Ventilate the oven to cool the pans.
Transfer cooled pans to the planting room and let them remain there for approximately 2.5 hours before depositing them in a barrel.

steps.title: Dry Sitotroga Cerealella Eggs
steps.instruction: Dry the washed eggs using a fan.

substeps.instruction: Place eggs in a tray containing an organza blanket and put the tray in the pantry.
Ventilate with a fan for approximately 2.5 hours.
Inspect and shake the eggs every 20 minutes to ensure uniform drying.

steps.title: Incubate Sitotroga Cerealella Eggs
steps.instruction: Incubate eggs in sterilized cups to allow larvae emergence.

substeps.instruction: Disinfect plastic cups with alcohol.
Deposit 4 grams of eggs per cup.
Incubate for an average of 24 hours.
Inspect every 12 hours to monitor larvae emergence.

steps.title: Disinfect Sowing Frames
steps.instruction: Clean and sterilize the three-cell frames used for sowing.

substeps.instruction: Wash frames with water and detergent.
Immerse frames in chlorine and allow them to air dry.
Disinfect frames with alcohol before moving them to the planting room.

steps.title: Sow Larvae and Eggs
steps.instruction: Infect the sterilized wheat substrate with larvae and eggs.

substeps.instruction: Fill each of the three cells in a frame with 2 kg of sterilized wheat (6 kg total per frame).
Once larvae emergence is verified, plant larvae and eggs into the frames.
Place 4 grams of eggs (from an incubation cup) into each cell (12 grams total per frame).
Label frames with masking tape (batch number, frame number, shelf number) and transfer to the incubation room.
Maintain abiotic conditions at 25°C and 75-86% relative humidity for 20-25 days until the larval stage reaches pupa.

steps.title: Prepare Emersion Cabinets
steps.instruction: Prepare and disinfect cabinets for adult emersion based on lining material.

substeps.instruction: For organza-lined cabinets: Wash with water and detergent, dry, and disinfect with chlorine and alcohol.
For bridal fabric-lined cabinets: Wash with water and detergent, install bridal fabric to seal all openings, disinfect edges with chlorine, and then disinfect with alcohol.
Install a plastic funnel using masking tape leading to a porrón (capture jar) at the bottom.

steps.title: Prepare Porrones
steps.instruction: Clean and disinfect the capture jars (porrones).

substeps.instruction: Wash used porrones with water, detergent, and chlorine.
Disinfect porrones with chlorine and alcohol before use.
Identify each porrón by cabinet number, porrón number, and date of placement.

steps.title: Collect Adult Emergence
steps.instruction: Transfer pupae to cabinets and collect emerging adults.

substeps.instruction: Place pupae frames in cabinets according to batch order (capacity: 10 frames per cabinet).
Allow emersion for 30 to 35 days maximum.
Collect adults deposited in the capture porrón at the bottom of the funnel, replacing the porrón as needed.

steps.title: Prepare Oviposition Equipment
steps.instruction: Clean and prepare frames and trays for egg collection.

substeps.instruction: Wash oviposition frames and egg deposit sheets with detergent, water, and chlorine.
Disinfect with alcohol and chlorine.
Line the oviposition frame with organza fabric on both sides and place it in the egg deposit tray.

steps.title: Clean Adults and Eggs
steps.instruction: Remove debris from the captured adults and eggs.

substeps.instruction: Transfer porrones to a cleaning area with an extractor.
Perform non-abrupt movements to remove dust or scale until only adults and eggs remain in the jar.
Weigh the adults and eggs, then weigh the empty porrón.

steps.title: Extract and Store Eggs
steps.instruction: Collect eggs from adults and store them by maturity.

substeps.instruction: Transfer adults and eggs into oviposition frames and trays.
Use a brush to remove eggs from the bottom of the porrón.
Harvest eggs daily and clean them using a cell.
Classify eggs by maturity: white/fresh eggs for Trichogramma breeding and red eggs for chrysopas breeding.
Refrigerate finished product for 15 days at 10-15°C.
